problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(x,z)\,:\,\boxed{}\,}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the part of the surface $y=\frac{1}{xz}$ that lies inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2.$ From left to right, what are the missing expressions?

examples.knowledge_point: Surface Areas of Surfaces Defined as X=F(Y,Z) or Y=F(X,Z)
examples.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the plane $x =y+\sqrt 2 z$ whose projection onto the $yz$-plane is bounded by the constraints $1 \leq y\leq 2$ and $1 \leq z \leq 3.$
examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $x=f(y,z)$ with $(y,z)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \,  \text{d}S = \iint\limits_D \sqrt{1+\left(\dfrac{\partial x}{\partial y}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{\partial x}{\partial z}\right)^2} \: \text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
x = y+\sqrt 2 z, \qquad (y,z)\in D,
$$

where 

$$
D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 1 \leq y \leq 2, \: 1 \leq z \leq 3\big\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066535/assets/240ac546b0dd725e392dd0bd475b2ef00eebce2594be5921285e227137538c46.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y+\sqrt{2}z)=1, \\ \frac{∂x}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(y+\sqrt{2}z)=\sqrt{2},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂x}{∂y})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂x}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{4}\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =2\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =2\cdot (2-1)\cdot (3-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the surface area of the portion of the surface $z=3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}y$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}y,\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{sin}⁡2x},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066535/assets/f6200343142274ee2f5b3934cbe014ee24edf8177f3a544c38dc070bb7df83ef.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}y)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡x, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}y)=2\sqrt{2},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(3\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+9{cos}^{2}⁡x+8}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{9(1+{cos}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡x}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\cdot y\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $u=1+{cos}^{2}⁡x,$ we get $\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x.$ Also, the limits must be changed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & \frac{\pi }{2} \\ u & 2 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Substituting these into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{2}^{1}\sqrt{u}(-\text{d}u) \\  & =3{\int }_{1}^{2}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2{u}^{3/2}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2({2}^{3/2}-1) \\  & =4\sqrt{2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$
